headlines.title: RTX Locks In a Decade of Defense Dominance
headlines.summary: RTX's Raytheon unit won an $8 billion nuclear command-and-control contract and a $729 million counter-drone export deal, bolstering long-term revenue visibility as its stock trades below recent highs.

headlines.title: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell RTX Stock Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
headlines.summary: RTX heads into Q3 earnings with strong aerospace and defense demand, a record backlog and attractive valuation, despite lingering supply-chain challenges.

headlines.title: Defense ETFs in Spotlight Ahead of Q3 Earnings Season
headlines.summary: Defense ETFs draw attention ahead of Q3 earnings as rising Treasury yields pressure valuations, while strong demand may support growth.

headlines.title: Lockheed Martin or RTX? The Dividend Difference Investors Shouldn’t Ignore
headlines.summary: Lockheed Martin and RTX both raised full-year guidance on the same July morning, but their balance sheets and business mixes tell two very different stories about which dividend survives a budget freeze or a single bad program charge.

headlines.title: RTX (RTX) Could Be 19% Undervalued On Fresh Defense Contract Wins
headlines.summary: RTX (RTX) has been in focus after Raytheon secured a five year contract worth up to US$6.3b for Standard Missile 3 Block IB interceptors, alongside US$729m in counter drone system orders. RTX shares trade at US$186.47 and have gained 1.88% on a 1 day share price return and 3.45% over the past week, even though the 30 day share price return is down 4.54% and the 90 day share price return is down 4.06%. description: RTX Corporation, an aerospace and defense company, provides systems and services for commercial, military, and government customers worldwide. It operates through three segments: Collins Aerospace (Collins), Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. The Collins segment offers aerospace and defense products, and aftermarket services for civil and military aircraft manufacturers and commercial airlines, as well as regional, business, and general aviation, defense, and commercial space operations. This segment designs, manufactures, and supplies electric power generation and management and distribution, environmental control, flight control, air data and aircraft sensing, engine control, and engine nacelle systems, as well as engine components; cabin interiors, including seating, oxygen, food and beverage preparation, storage and galley, lavatory, and wastewater management systems; connected aviation solutions and services; and systems solutions for connected battlespace, test and training range systems, crew escape systems, and simulation and training. It also provides spare parts, overhaul and repair, engineering and technical support, training and fleet management solutions, and asset and information management services. The Pratt & Whitney segment supplies aircraft engines for commercial, military, business jet, and general aviation customers; and produces, sells, and services military and commercial auxiliary power units, as well as offers fleet management and aftermarket maintenance, repair, and overhaul services. The Raytheon segment provides defensive and offensive threat detection, tracking, and mitigation capabilities for government and commercial customers. This segment offers sensors, mission orchestration and satellite control products, and software. The company was formerly known as Raytheon Technologies Corporation and changed its name to RTX Corporation in July 2023. RTX Corporation was incorporated in 1934 and is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
